Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT 01 June 2009 DIRECTOR MERILO Q. UMBARO City Director DILG-Region City Government Operations Office Rm. 16, City Hall Davao City Dear Director Limbaro: This has reference to your earlier letter requesting for a prompt and immediate legal opinion regarding the "irrevocable resignation" previously tendered by Mayor Rodrigo R. Duterte as deputized representative of the National Police Commission (NAPOLCOM) in order to give the Commission on Human Rights (CHR) a free hand and undue influence over the on-going public inquiry/investigation on the alleged extra-judicial killing in Davao City. Hence, you want to seek guidance on the following issues, which we quoted in toto: "(1) Can the Mayor resign/ abdicate his being a NAPOLCOM deputy in the matter of operational supervision and control over the PNPP (2) If no, can he be cited for dereliction or abandonment of duty under the Local Code and RA 6975 as amended by RA 8551.2„ On your part, you entertained the idea that the Mayor can abdicate or relinquish his deputation in conjunction to Section 65 of RA 8551 According to you, since deputation can be withdrawn by the grantor, which is the NAPOLCOM, there is no reason that same grant of authority may be

-2- waived or formally relinquished to the grantor who in return shall automatically exercise such function of administrative control and operational supervision over the police pursuant to its mandate under Section 14 of RA 6975, as amended. Your view was further bolstered by the absence of a provision under RA 6975 and RA 8551 providing for the resignation of the NAPOLCOM deputized representative. With all due respect to your view, we have a different stand on the matter. Section 14 (a) of Republic Act 6975, otherwise known as the "Department of the Interior and Local Government Act of 1990"" provides that the NAPOLCOM shall exercise administrative control over the Philippine National Police. This was thereafter amended by Republic Act 8551, otherwise known as the "Philippine National Police Refbrm and Reorganization Act OF 1998" when it is provided under Section 5 therein that the NAPOLCOM shall exercise administrative control and operational supervision over the Philippine National Police. Corollarily, governors and mayors are deputized under Section 51 of RA 6975 as representatives of the NAPOLCOM in their respective territorial jurisdiction. In fact, this duty of the local chief executives, the city mayors in particular, is reiterated under Section 455 (b)(2)(v) of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160), thus: "Section 455. Chief Executive; Powers, Duties and Compensation. (b) For efficient, effective and economical governance the purpose Of Which is the general welfare Of the city and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the city mayor shall: (2) Enforce all laws and ordinances relative to the governance of the city and in the exercise of the appropriate corporate powers provided for under Section 22 of this Code, implement all approved policies, programs, projects, services and activities of the city and, in addition to the foregoing, shall: (v) Act as the deputized representative of the National Police Commission, formulate the peace and order plan of the city and upon I its approval, irnplement the same; and as such

-3- exercise general and operational control and supervision over the local police forces in the city, in accordance with R.A. No. 6975;" Such deputation is further reinforced under Section 64 of RA 8551 when this deputation of local chief executives as NAPOLCOM representatives is made automatic, that is, made simultaneous to their assumption into office. Said provision states and we quote: of LO "SECTION 64. Automatic Deputation Government Executives as Commxssxon Representatives. Governors and mayors. upon having been elected and having gualified as such, are automatically deputized as representatives of the National Police Commission in their As deputized agents of the respective jurisdiction. Commission, local government executives can inspect police forces and units, conduct audit, and exercise other functions as may be duly authorized by the Commission." (Emphasis Supplied) In view of the foregoing, it is thus clear that by virtue of his being the Mayor of Davao City, Mayor Duterte also became the deputized representative of NAPOLCOM in that locality. Such duty has been made part of the many duties of the City Mayor so that whoever is the incumbent to said position is also mandated to act as the deputized representative of the NAPOLCOM, such duty having been conferred by RA 6975, as reiterated under Section 455 (b)(2)(v) of the Local Government Code of 1991. Along this line, may we emphasize that a •public office" is defined as the right, authority or duty, created and conferred by law, by which for a Wiven period, either fixed by law or enduring at the pleasure of the creating power, an individual is invested with some soverezg-n poweri of government to be exercised by him for the benefit of the public [Fernandez vs. Sto. Tomas, G.R. No. 116418, 07 March 19952. The duties of the City Mayor that make up his total sovereign power can be found primarily the Local Government Code of 1991, particularly Section 455 thereof and in other scattered provisions thereof, and also in other pertinent laws. Hence, Mayor Duterte cannot, by tendering an "irrevocable resignation" as deputized representative of NAPOLCOM, abdicate and relinquish a portion of his mandated duties conferred by the sovereign authority to the position of a City Mayor. His irrevocable resignation earlier tendered can be construed as an act of abdicating a portion of his

-4- sovereign power conferred by the sovereign authority and may thus give rise to a possible dereliction of duty, which is one of the grounds for disciplinary action against local elective officials under Section 60 of the Local Government Code of 1991. The only time when he ceases to become a deputized representative of the NAPOLCOM is when he also ceases to be the Mayor of Davao City or if the same is withdrawn pursuant to Section 52 of RA 6975, as amended by Section 65 of RA 8551. While the purpose of his "irrevocable resignation" as NAPOLCOM deputy is noble, that is, in order to give the CHR a free hand and undue influence over the on-going public inquiry/investigation on the alleged extra-judicial killing in Davao City, the same is not in accordance with the aforequoted provisions of law for reasons already given above. Moreover, on the issue of NAPOLCOM as the grantor of the authority of the governors and mayors as NAPOLCOM representatives, please be informed that a careful reading of the aforementioned Section 51 of RA 6975 and the aforequoted Section 64 of RA 8551 would reveal that the NAPOLCOM is not the grantor thereof. It is the law itself, RA 6975 in relation to Section 455(b)(2)(v) of the Local Government Code of 1991 which conferred unto and constituted the governors and mayors as NAPOLCOM representatives. And Section 64 of RA 8551 made such deputation of governors and mayors as automatic, that is, upon having been elected and having qualified to their respective positions or simultaneous to the time of their assumption into office, governors or mayors are automatically constituted as deputized NAPOLCOM agents. Hence, upon the arrival of that time, the governors and mayors are no longer required to execute other operative act before they can act as deputized agents of NAPOLCOM. On the other hand, the provision of Section 52 of RA 6975, as amended by Section 65 of RA 8551, regarding withdrawal of deputation is just a legal remedy provided for by law in case there is a ground to withdraw the same. As stated in our recital of facts, your idea of the NAPOLCOM, as grantor of the authority of the governors and mayors as NAPOLCOM representatives, is inferred from Section 65 of RA 8551, which authorizes the NAPOLCOM to suspend or withdraw the deputation of any local executive under certain conditions. Perhaps, you have drawn this from the logic that NAPOLCOM cannot suspend or withdraw what it did not, in the first place, grant. Section 65 of RA 8551 provides and we quote: "SEC. 65. Section 52 of Republic Act No. 6975 is hereby amended to read as follows:

-5- "SEC. 52. Suspension or Withdrawal of Deputation. — Unless reversed by the President, the Commission may, after consultation with the provincial governor and congressman concerned, suspend or withdraw the deputation of any local executive for any Of the following grounds: "(a) Frequent unauthorized absences; "(b) Abuse of authority; Providing material support to criminal elements; or "(d) Engaging in acts inimical to national security or which negate the effectiveness of the peace and order campaign. "Upon good cause shown, the President may, directly or through the Commission, motu proprio restore such deputation withdrawn from any local executive. Following your idea, we deemed it proper to go back and examine the old provision of Section 52 of RA 6975, which provides and we quote: "SEC. 52. Suspension or Withdrawal of Deputation. — The President may. upon consultation with the provincial governor and congressman concerned. suspend the power of operational supervision and control of any local executive over poliqe units assigned or stationed in his jurisdiction for any of the following grounds: Frequent unauthorized absences; "(b) Abuse of authority; "(c) Providing material support to criminal elements; or "(d) Engaging in acts inimical to national security or which negate the effectiveness of the peace and order campaign. "Upon good cause shown, the President may, motu proprio or upon recommendation of the National Police Commission, restore such power withdrawn from any local executive." (Emphasis Supplied) We can see from the old provision that the President of the Republic of the Philippines originally exercised the power of suspension. In the new or amendatory provision of Section 65 of RA 8551, the power of suspension or withdrawal is now given to the NAPOLCOM, subject only to

-6- any reversal made by the President. The change on who will exercise the power of suspension, that is, from the President to the NAPOLCOM only confirms our view that the NAPOLCOM is not the grantor of the authority of the governors and mayors as NAPOLCOM representatives. It was the law as cited above which granted such authority and provided for the manner of suspension or withdrawal subject to the amendment made under RA 8551. We hope that we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADER Undersecretary Director Quirtno M. Libunao, CESO Ill Regional Director Region Xl, Davao City Legal:17
